title: Thread lifecycle and states
context: What are the states of a Java thread's lifecycle?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Java concurrency questions (1 of 3)
source.note: Translated and condensed into English; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: `Thread.State` has six values. NEW is created but not started. RUNNABLE means it is running or ready to run on the JVM; the OS decides when it gets a CPU. BLOCKED waits to enter a synchronized block or method. WAITING waits without a timeout, for example in wait(), join() or LockSupport.park. TIMED_WAITING does the same with a timeout, as in sleep(). TERMINATED means run has finished or an exception ended it. start() moves NEW to RUNNABLE, and a thread can be started only once.

points.title: Six states
points.why: Interview answers need NEW, RUNNABLE, BLOCKED, WAITING, TIMED_WAITING and TERMINATED.

points.title: Blocked versus waiting
points.why: BLOCKED is waiting for a monitor lock. WAITING is waiting for another thread's signal.

points.title: start once
points.why: Calling start twice throws IllegalThreadStateException. Call run only to run code in the current thread.
